questions.stem: Patch, a frequent shopper at Soon-Shop Stores, received a rain check for an advertised sale item after Soon-Shop's supply of the product ran out. The rain check was in writing and stated that the item would be offered to the customer at the advertised sale price for an unspecified period of time. A Soon-Shop employee signed the rain check. When Patch returned to the store one month later to purchase the item, the store refused to honor the rain check. Under the Sales Article of the UCC, will Patch win a suit to enforce the rain check?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No, because one month is too long a time for a rain check to be effective.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No, because the rain check did not state the effective time period necessary to keep the offer open.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes, because Soon-Shop is required to have sufficient supplies of the sale item to satisfy all customers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yes, because the rain check met the requirements of a merchant's firm offer even though no effective time period was stated.

questions.explanation:
A firm offer is a term or condition to a sales contract that cannot be revoked.

A firm offer is created when the SUM conditions (signed, up to three months, and merchant) are met.

Signed: The offeror must specifically sign a written offer on the page containing the offer.

Up to three months: The offer is enforceable for the time specified in the writing. However, there is no requirement that a time be specified ("No, because the rain check did not state the effective time period ne…"). If no time is specified, then it is open for a reasonable time, but no longer than three months ("No, because one month is too long a time for a rain check to be effec…").

Merchant: The offeror must be a merchant.

There is no rule requiring a merchant to maintain a sufficient inventory of sales items to meet all potential customer demand ("Yes, because Soon-Shop is required to have sufficient supplies of the…"). However, when merchants run out of sale item inventory, they often issue a rain check to the disappointed customers. A rain check functions as a firm offer because it is in writing and made by a merchant. A rain check typically contains an expiration date, but that is not a requirement. In this case, one month is considered a reasonable time.

Note:

A rain check is a promise or commitment from a seller to a buyer that an item currently out of stock can be purchased at a later date for the current day's sale price.

Rain checks are most commonly issued by retail stores. When advertising a sale, a retailer is required to honor the discounted price of a product even when supplies run out. Customers can request a rain check--usually in the form of a paper voucher--if they are unable to purchase the advertised item during the Sale period. Most rain checks are valid for 30, 60, or 90 days, depending on the store.
The time that a firm offer (rain check) remains open is usually specified; however, there is no requirement that a time be given. If no time is specified, then it is open for a reasonable time, but no longer than three months.
questions.explanationJa: 確定申込み（firm offer）は撤回できない申込みであり、署名（Signed）、最長3か月（Up to three months）、商人（Merchant）の条件（SUM）を満たすと成立する。申込みが有効な期間は書面で定めた期間だが、期間を定めることは要件ではなく、定めがない場合は合理的な期間（ただし3か月以内）有効となる。雨天引換券（rain check）は商人が書面で行い従業員が署名したものなので確定申込みとして機能し、本問の1か月は合理的な期間内である。したがって、有効期間の記載がなくてもPatchは勝訴する。なお、商人が全顧客の需要を満たすだけの在庫を持つ義務はない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.1

questions.stem: Which of the following contracts is handled under common law rules rather than under Article 2 of the Uniform Commercial Code?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Oral contract to have hair styled in which expensive products will be used on the hair.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oral contract to purchase a textbook for $100.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Written contract to purchase an old handcrafted chair for $600 from a private party.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Written contract to purchase a heater from a dealer to be installed by the buyer in her home.

questions.explanation:
Article 2 of the UCC (Uniform Commercial Code) deals with contracts for the sale of goods (tangible personal property). When there are no specific provisions in the UCC, the rules of common law apply. The seller of the goods may be a merchant or a nonmerchant ("Written contract to purchase an old handcrafted chair for $600 from a…"). A merchant deals in the goods involved in the transaction.

UCC Article 2 does not apply to contracts involving real property or services. When the contract is for both goods and service, Article 2 will not apply when the goods are incidental to the services (eg, hair products used when styling hair). However, Article 2 applies when the services are incidental to or a necessary part of the purchase of goods (eg, installing a purchased heater) ("Written contract to purchase a heater from a dealer to be installed b…").

("Oral contract to purchase a textbook for $100.") There is no minimum amount required in order for a sales contract to be covered by UCC Article 2. Therefore, an oral contract for a sale of goods (a textbook) for $100 is covered by UCC Article 2.
questions.explanationJa: UCC第2編は物品（有体動産）の売買契約を扱い、売主が商人か非商人かは問わない。不動産や役務の契約には第2編は適用されず、コモンローが適用される。物品と役務の両方を含む契約では、物品が役務に付随するもの（髪のスタイリングで使う整髪料など）であれば第2編は適用されないため、高価な製品を使う髪のスタイリングの口頭契約はコモンローで扱われる。一方、役務が物品購入に付随するもの（買主が自分で設置するヒーターの購入）であれば第2編が適用される。また、第2編の適用に最低金額はないので、$100の教科書の口頭契約も第2編の対象である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.2

questions.stem: An appliance seller promised a restaurant owner that a home dishwasher would fulfill the dishwashing requirements of a large restaurant. The dishwasher was purchased, but it was not powerful enough for the restaurant. Under the Sales Article of the UCC, what warranty was violated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The implied warranty of marketability.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The implied warranty of merchantability.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The express warranty that the goods conform to the seller's promise.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The express warranty against infringement.

questions.explanation:
When goods are sold, the seller makes certain promises to the buyer that the buyer can legally enforce if needed. These promises are known as warranties, and there are two basic types: express and implied.

Express warranties are specific statements made by the seller that become the basis for the bargain.

Implied warranties refer to promises that are present (arise) as a matter of law. Therefore, there is no need for the seller to make any specialized warranty-like statement, either oral or written ("The implied warranty of merchantability.").

In this scenario, an express warranty exists because the seller specifically promised that the dishwasher had enough power to meet the needs of a large restaurant, and the buyer purchased it based on that promise. Since the dishwasher did not perform as promised, that express warranty was violated.
questions.explanationJa: 物品の売買では、売主は買主が法的に強制できる約束（保証）をしており、保証には明示の保証と黙示の保証がある。明示の保証は、売主が行った具体的な表明で取引の基礎となったものであり、黙示の保証は売主が何も表明しなくても法律上当然に生じるものである。本問では、売主が「この食器洗い機は大規模レストランの需要を満たす能力がある」と具体的に約束し、買主はその約束に基づいて購入している。食器洗い機が約束どおりの性能を発揮しなかったので、物品が売主の約束に適合するという明示の保証に違反したことになる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.3

questions.stem: High sues the manufacturer, wholesaler, and retailer for bodily injuries caused by a power saw High purchased. Which of the following statements is correct under strict liability theory?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Contributory negligence on High's part will always be a bar to recovery.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The manufacturer will avoid liability if it can show it followed the custom of the industry.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Privity will be a bar to recovery insofar as the wholesaler is concerned if the wholesaler did not have a reasonable opportunity to inspect.

choices.label: D
choices.text: High may recover even if he cannot show any negligence was involved.

questions.explanation:
Choice "High may recover even if he cannot show any negligence was involved." (Correct): Strict liability applies without any need to prove negligence on the part of the defendant but rather that the product was defective and that damages occurred because of the defect. Contributory negligence would only bar recovery if High intentionally misused the product. Reliance on the customary practices of an industry is a viable defense in a negligence case, but not in a suit based on strict liability. Privity of contract is not required in a product liability case involving personal injuries or illness.

Choice "Contributory negligence on High's part will always be a bar to recove…" (Incorrect): Strict liability applies without any need to prove negligence on the part of the defendant but rather that the product was defective and that damages occurred because of the defect. Contributory negligence would only bar recovery if High intentionally misused the product.

Choice "The manufacturer will avoid liability if it can show it followed the…" (Incorrect): Strict liability applies without any need to prove negligence on the part of the defendant but rather that the product was defective and that damages occurred because of the defect. Reliance on the customary practices of an industry is a viable defense in a negligence case, but not in a suit based on strict liability.

Choice "Privity will be a bar to recovery insofar as the wholesaler is concer…" (Incorrect): Strict liability applies without any need to prove negligence on the part of the defendant but rather that the product was defective and that damages occurred because of the defect. Privity of contract is not required in a product liability case involving personal injuries or illness.
questions.explanationJa: 厳格責任（strict liability）では、被告の過失を証明する必要はなく、製品に欠陥があり、その欠陥によって損害が生じたことを示せば足りる。したがって、Highは過失を一切証明できなくても損害を回復できる。原告の寄与過失は、Highが製品を意図的に誤用した場合にしか回復の障害にならない。業界の慣行に従ったことは過失訴訟では抗弁になり得るが、厳格責任では抗弁にならず、人身傷害を伴う製造物責任ではprivity（契約関係）も要求されない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.4

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, which of the following statements is correct regarding risk of loss and title to the goods under a sale or return contract?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Title and risk of loss are shared equally between the buyer and the seller.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Title remains with the seller until the buyer approves or accepts the goods, but risk of loss passes to the buyer immediately following delivery of the goods to the buyer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Title and risk of loss remain with the seller until the buyer pays for the goods.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Title and risk of loss rest with the buyer until the goods are returned to the seller.

questions.explanation:
A common type of sale contract is a conditional sale in which the buyer is given the option to cancel the contract and return the goods. One type of conditional sales contract is a sale or return contract. This is a contract in which the buyer/merchant is acquiring the goods for resale and is given the right to cancel the contract if it is unable to resell the goods. After the buyer receives the goods and then holds them for resale to customers, the title and risk of loss rests with the buyer.

If the buyer chooses to return the unsold goods, then the same rules apply as in a normal sales contract in which the rules for passage of title and risk of loss are based on the shipping terms. Under those shipping terms, title and risk of loss may be with either the buyer or the seller depending on if the shipping terms are FOB destination, FOB shipping point, or hold for pickup ("Title and risk of loss are shared equally between the buyer and the s…" / "Title remains with the seller until the buyer approves or accepts the…" / "Title and risk of loss remain with the seller until the buyer pays fo…").
questions.explanationJa: 条件付き売買の一種である返品条件付き売買（sale or return）は、買主（商人）が再販売のために物品を取得し、売れなかった場合に契約を解除して返品できる契約である。買主が物品を受け取り顧客への再販売のために保有している間は、所有権と危険負担は買主にある。買主が売れ残った物品を返品する場合は、通常の売買と同様に、出荷条件（FOB仕向地、FOB出荷地点、引取り）に従って所有権と危険負担が移転する。したがって、所有権と危険負担は物品が売主に返品されるまで買主にある。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.5

questions.stem: With respect to the sale of goods, the warranty of title

choices.label: A
choices.text: Applies only if the seller is a merchant.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Applies only if the seller expressly makes the warranty.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Provides that there are no undisclosed liens or other claims on the goods.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Can be disclaimed by a merchant who sells the goods "as is."

questions.explanation:
The warranty of title (WOT) is an implied warranty for all types of sales, not just sales by merchants ("Applies only if the seller is a merchant."). Under the WOT, the seller guarantees that it has good title to the product and there are no undisclosed claims (eg, product is not stolen). In addition, the seller promises that the transfer to the buyer does not infringe on the rights of any third party (eg, no patent infringement).

The WOT can be disclaimed in all types of sales regardless of the purchaser's status. However, the disclaimer must be very specific ("seller specifically disclaims the warranty of title"). General disclaimers ("as is," "with all faults") are not sufficient ("Can be disclaimed by a merchant who sells the goods "as is."").
questions.explanationJa: 権原の保証（warranty of title）は、商人による売買に限らずすべての売買で生じる黙示の保証である。この保証により、売主は自らが物品について正当な権原を有し、開示されていない担保権その他の請求権が存在しないこと（盗品でないことなど）を保証する。あわせて、買主への移転が第三者の権利（特許など）を侵害しないことも約束する。権原の保証は放棄できるが、具体的に権原の保証を放棄すると明示する必要があり、「現状有姿（as is）」のような一般的な免責文言では足りない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.6

questions.stem: Thorn purchased a used entertainment system from Sound Corp. The sales contract stated that the entertainment system was being sold "as is." Under the Sales Article of the UCC, which of the following statements is correct regarding the Sound Corp's warranty of title?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Thorn and Sound Corp must be in privity of contract for the warranty of title to be effective.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The warranty of title automatically exists even though Sound Corp makes no specific reference to it in the sales contract.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Including the term "as is" in the sales contract is adequate communication for Sound Corp to disclaim the warranty of title.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The warranty of title may be disclaimed by Sound Corp at any time after the contract is formed.

questions.explanation:
The warranty of title (WOT) is an implied warranty that arises as a matter of law in every sale of goods. Therefore, it does not need to be explicitly mentioned by the seller during the sales process.

If the seller does not want the WOT to apply to the sale, then the seller can disclaim it. However, it must be disclaimed prior to completing the sale ("The warranty of title may be disclaimed by Sound Corp at any time aft…"). In addition, the disclaimer must specifically say that the WOT is being disclaimed. Saying the goods are being sold "as is" or "with all fault" is effective only when disclaiming the warranty of merchantability, not the WOT ("Including the term "as is" in the sales contract is adequate communic…").

These stringent disclaimer rules protect buyers who might not be willing to pay the same price (or make the purchase at all) if they know the seller will not guarantee clean title and therefore the goods might be stolen property.

("Thorn and Sound Corp must be in privity of contract for the warranty…") There is no requirement that the buyer and seller be in privity of contract for the WOT to be effective.
questions.explanationJa: 権原の保証は、すべての物品売買で法律上当然に生じる黙示の保証であるため、売主が売買契約で特に言及しなくても自動的に存在する。売主が権原の保証を適用させたくない場合は放棄できるが、売買の完了前に、権原の保証を放棄すると具体的に明示しなければならない。「現状有姿（as is）」や「一切の瑕疵を含めて」という文言は商品性の保証の放棄には有効だが、権原の保証の放棄には不十分である。また、権原の保証が有効となるために買主と売主の間にprivityは必要ない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.7

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, which of the following statements is correct regarding a seller's obligation under a F.O.B. destination contract?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The seller is required to arrange for the buyer to pick up the conforming goods at a specified destination.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The seller is required to tender delivery of conforming goods at a specified destination.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The seller is required to tender delivery of conforming goods at the buyer's place of business.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The seller is required to tender delivery of conforming goods to a carrier who delivers to a destination specified by the buyer.

questions.explanation:
FOB stands for free on board. It is a shipping term that indicates the point at which legal title to shipped goods is transferred from the seller to the buyer.

There are two types of FOB designations:

In an FOB shipping point contract, the seller is required to tender delivery of conforming goods to a carrier (at the seller's loading dock). Legal title passes from the seller to the buyer at that time. The carrier then delivers the goods to a location designated by the buyer ("The seller is required to tender delivery of conforming goods to a ca…").

In an FOB destination point contract, the seller is required to tender delivery of conforming goods at a specified destination. Legal title passes from the seller to the buyer when the buyer takes possession of the goods from the transportation carrier (tendered by the carrier to the buyer).

("The seller is required to arrange for the buyer to pick up the confor…") The agreement by which the seller arranges for the buyer to pick up the conforming goods at a specified destination is a hold for pickup contract.

("The seller is required to tender delivery of conforming goods at the…") An FOB destination point contract does not always require that the goods be delivered to the buyer's place of business, even though that is often what occurs.
questions.explanationJa: FOB仕向地（destination）契約では、売主は指定された仕向地で契約に適合した物品の引渡しを提供しなければならない。これに対し、FOB出荷地点（shipping point）契約では、売主は適合物品を運送人に引き渡せばよく、その後運送人が買主の指定した場所へ運ぶ。売主が指定場所で買主に物品を引き取らせる取決めは引取り（hold for pickup）契約である。また、FOB仕向地契約は、実際にはそうなることが多いものの、必ずしも買主の営業所への引渡しを要求するものではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.8

questions.stem: ABC Corp. contracts with JCN Inc. to sell JCN 3,000 widgets under 60-day credit terms. The widgets are to be shipped to JCN's warehouse. The contract reads, "Shipping terms: FOB Destination. Buyer assumes risk of loss when Seller tenders goods to freight carrier." En route to JCN's warehouse, the carrier is involved in an accident and the widgets are destroyed. Under the UCC Sales Article, which company has legal title to the goods at the time of the accident?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ABC Corp. because the shipping terms are FOB destination.

choices.label: B
choices.text: JCN Inc. because the shipping terms are FOB destination.

choices.label: C
choices.text: ABC Corp. because JCN has not yet paid for the widgets.

choices.label: D
choices.text: JCN Inc. because the contract terms place risk of loss with the buyer.

questions.explanation:
FOB is a shipping term that indicates the point at which legal title to shipped goods is transferred from the seller (ABC Corp.) to the buyer (JCN Inc.).

There are two types of FOB designations:

FOB shipping point, in which legal title passes from the seller to the buyer when the goods are delivered to the third-party transportation carrier, usually at the seller's loading dock.

FOB destination point, in which legal title passes from the seller to the buyer when the buyer takes possession of the goods from the transportation carrier ("JCN Inc. because the shipping terms are FOB destination.").

Under the UCC, title to goods is distinguished from the liabilities (risk of loss) associated with those goods. Therefore, it is possible for one party (ABC Corp., seller) to have title to the goods during shipment (FOB destination) while another party (JCN, Inc., buyer) has the risk of loss during shipment ("JCN Inc. because the contract terms place risk of loss with the buyer.").

("ABC Corp. because JCN has not yet paid for the widgets.") ABC retains title because of the FOB destination shipping terms and not because JCN has not yet paid for the goods.
questions.explanationJa: FOBは、出荷された物品の法的所有権が売主から買主に移転する時点を示す出荷条件である。FOB仕向地では、買主が運送人から物品を受け取った時点で所有権が移転するため、輸送中の事故の時点では所有権は売主のABCにある。UCCでは所有権と危険負担は区別されており、本問のように契約で買主が運送人への引渡し時から危険を負担すると定めても、所有権は出荷条件に従って売主に残る。また、ABCが所有権を保持しているのは出荷条件がFOB仕向地だからであり、JCNが代金を支払っていないからではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.9

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, which of the following events will release the buyer from all its obligations under a sales contract?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Destruction of the goods after risk of loss passed to the buyer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Receipt of nonconforming goods by the buyer who promptly notified the seller.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Anticipatory repudiation by the buyer that is retracted before the seller cancels the contract.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Refusal of the seller to give written assurance of performance when reasonably demanded by the buyer.

questions.explanation:
Anticipatory breach (anticipatory repudiation) of contract occurs when it doesn't appear that one party to the contract will perform the contract. At this point, the wronged party can request assurance of the other party's ability to perform the contract. If the other party fails or refuses to assure performance, the wronged party can cancel the contract and sue for damages. At that point, the buyer is relieved of all contractual obligations.

("Destruction of the goods after risk of loss passed to the buyer.") Once risk of loss has passed to the buyer, it is the buyer's obligation to pay for the goods even if they are subsequently destroyed.

("Receipt of nonconforming goods by the buyer who promptly notified the…") Nonconforming goods do not relieve the buyer of all its obligations under a sales contract. If the buyer receives nonconforming goods, then the buyer should inform the seller. The seller then has the right to cure by sending conforming goods by the original contract date or within a reasonable time after learning the goods do not conform.

("Anticipatory repudiation by the buyer that is retracted before the se…") Anticipatory repudiation by the buyer that is later retracted will not relieve the buyer of its obligations under the contract.
questions.explanationJa: 履行期前の履行拒絶（anticipatory repudiation）は、相手方が契約を履行しないと見込まれる場合に生じ、被害を受ける当事者は相手方に履行の保証を求めることができる。相手方が保証を拒んだり提供しなかったりすれば、被害当事者は契約を解除して損害賠償を請求でき、買主は契約上のすべての義務から解放される。危険負担が買主に移転した後に物品が滅失しても、買主は代金を支払う義務を負う。不適合品を受け取って売主に通知しても、売主には適合品で補完（cure）する権利があるため買主の義務は消滅せず、買主自身の履行拒絶を撤回した場合も買主の義務は残る。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.10

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, which of the following statements is correct regarding risk of loss and title to the goods under a sale on approval contract?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Title and risk of loss are shared equally between the buyer and the seller.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Title and risk of loss remain with the seller until the goods have been accepted by the buyer or the approval period has elapsed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Title and risk of loss remain with the seller until the buyer pays for the goods.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Title remains with the seller until the buyer approves or accepts the goods, but risk of loss passes to the buyer immediately following delivery of the goods to the buyer.

questions.explanation: In sale on approval contracts, title and risk of loss remain with the seller until the buyer accepts the goods explicitly or the approval period elapses. As a result, the buyer does not have title to the goods or risk of loss until the goods are accepted
questions.explanationJa: 試用売買（sale on approval）では、所有権と危険負担は、買主が明示的に物品を承認するか承認期間が経過するまで売主にとどまる。したがって、買主は物品を承認するまで所有権も危険負担も負わない。物品の引渡しや代金の支払いではなく、買主の承認（または承認期間の経過）が移転の基準となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.11

questions.stem: Which of the following factors results in an express warranty with respect to a sale of goods?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The seller's description of the goods as part of the basis of the bargain.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The seller selects goods knowing the buyer's intended use.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The seller's statement that the goods are being sold "as is."

choices.label: D
choices.text: The seller's written statement that the goods will perform better than any similar goods.

questions.explanation:
When goods are sold, a seller makes certain promises to a buyer that the buyer can legally enforce if necessary. These promises are known as warranties and come in two basic types: express and implied.

Express warranties are specific oral or written statements made by the seller that become the basis for the bargain (sales negotiation and transaction). These include samples, models, or descriptions (promotional brochures) that describe how the goods will function. However, exaggerated "sales talk" claims ("best dishwasher ever made") are not express warranties ("The seller's written statement that the goods will perform better tha…")

Implied warranties are promises that are present as a matter of law. Therefore, there is no need for the seller to make any specialized warranty-like statement, either oral or written

In this scenario, an express warranty exists because the seller specifically describes how the goods will function in a certain way and the buyer purchases the goods based on that promise.

("The seller selects goods knowing the buyer's intended use.") The seller's selection of goods with knowledge of the buyer's intended use creates the implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose.

("The seller's statement that the goods are being sold "as is."") The seller's statement that the goods are being sold "as is" is a disclaimer of the implied warranty of fitness for particular purpose.
questions.explanationJa: 明示の保証とは、売主が行った具体的な口頭・書面の表明で取引の基礎となったものであり、見本、模型、物品の機能を説明する記述（宣伝パンフレットなど）が含まれる。したがって、取引の基礎の一部となった売主の物品の説明は明示の保証を生じさせる。一方、「他のどの類似品よりも性能が良い」のような誇張された売り込み文句は明示の保証に当たらない。買主の用途を知りながら売主が物品を選ぶことは特定目的適合性の黙示の保証を生じさせるものであり、「現状有姿（as is）」の表明は黙示の保証を放棄するものである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.12

questions.stem: Abel goes to the auto parts store and asks a clerk to help select the proper wrench for removing the engine mounts in a car that Abel is fixing up. Abel purchases the model suggested by the clerk and when opening the package discovers a document claiming to expressly disclaim warranties of title and merchantability. Able starts to take off the bolts and the wrench breaks after the first one. Abel's recourse against the store would most likely be based on what theory?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Negligence

choices.label: B
choices.text: Strict liability

choices.label: C
choices.text: Implied warranty of merchantability

choices.label: D
choices.text: Implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose

questions.explanation:
Choice "Implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose" (Correct): Even if other implied warranties are disclaimed, if the buyer has reasonably relied on the seller's judgment and skill in selection of the product, the seller may have impliedly warranted the good to be fit for a particular purpose. Here Abel relied on the sales clerk's recommendation of a particular model after informing the sales clerk of the purpose for which it would be used.

Choice "Negligence" (Incorrect): A negligence action must be brought against the actual tortfeasor; which would be the clerk, not the store. Negligence might apply if the clerk was careless in recommending the use of the wrench.

Choice "Strict liability" (Incorrect): Strict liability is a doctrine of tort law that allows recovery for damages suffered as a result of using a defective good. The wrench was not defective but, rather, was not suitable for use on the engine mounts Abel was using it for.

Choice "Implied warranty of merchantability" (Incorrect): The implied warranty of merchantability may be disclaimed. In this case, the product packaging expressly disclaimed the warranty of merchantability.
questions.explanationJa: 他の黙示の保証が放棄されていても、買主が売主の判断や技能を合理的に信頼して製品を選んだ場合、売主は特定目的適合性を黙示に保証したことになる。本問では、Abelが用途（エンジンマウントの取外し）を店員に伝え、店員の勧めたモデルを購入しているので、特定目的適合性の黙示の保証に基づいて店に請求するのが最も可能性が高い。商品性の黙示の保証は放棄が可能であり、本問では包装内の書面で明示的に放棄されている。また、レンチ自体に欠陥があったのではなく用途に適さなかっただけなので、欠陥製品による損害を対象とする厳格責任も当てはまらない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.13

questions.stem: Which of the following is not required by the UCC Sales Article for all sales contracts?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The contract must involve the sale of tangible personal property.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The obligations of merchants must be performed in good faith.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The obligations of nonmerchants must be performed in good faith.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The contract must involve the sale of goods for a price of $500 or more.

questions.explanation:
The UCC Sales Article (Article 2) regulates contracts for the sale of goods (tangible personal property). Under Article 2, both merchants and nonmerchants are required to perform their contractual obligations in good faith ("The obligations of merchants must be performed in good faith." / "The obligations of nonmerchants must be performed in good faith.").

For merchants, the good faith standard means that the merchant must act honestly and observe reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing in the trade (a rain check for out-of-stock advertised goods). For nonmerchants (usually the buyer), good faith means that the nonmerchant (as buyer) will accept conforming goods and pay for them as required in the contract.

Article 2 applies to all contracts involving sales of goods (tangible personal property), regardless of price ("The contract must involve the sale of tangible personal property."). The statute of frauds does not apply to all sales contracts. Instead, it contains a legal requirement that contracts for the sale of goods in the amount of $500 or more must be in writing to be enforceable.
questions.explanationJa: UCC売買編（第2編）は物品（有体動産）の売買契約を規律し、価格にかかわらずすべての物品売買契約に適用される。第2編の下では、商人も非商人も誠実に契約上の義務を履行しなければならない。商人にとっての誠実とは、正直に行動し取引における公正な取引の合理的な商慣行を守ることであり、非商人（通常は買主）にとっては、適合した物品を受領し契約どおり代金を支払うことである。$500以上の物品売買を書面で行わなければならないのは詐欺防止法の要件であり、すべての売買契約に求められるものではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.14

questions.stem: Under the UCC Sales Article, a plaintiff who proves fraud in the formation of a contract may

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elect to rescind the contract and need not return the consideration received from the other party.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Be entitled to rescind the contract and sue for damages resulting from the fraud.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Be entitled to punitive damages provided physical injuries resulted from the fraud.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rescind the contract even if there was no reliance on the fraudulent statement.

questions.explanation:
Choice "Be entitled to rescind the contract and sue for damages resulting fro…" (Correct): The contract may be rescinded because fraud was proven in the formation. Additionally the plaintiff may sue to recover damages that result from fraud.

Choice "Elect to rescind the contract and need not return the consideration r…" (Incorrect): The contract may be rescinded because fraud was proven in the formation. However when a contract is rescinded, the plaintiff cannot retain the consideration except to the extent these represent liquidated damages arising from the other party's actions.

Choice "Be entitled to punitive damages provided physical injuries resulted f…" (Incorrect): Punitive damages are not authorized under the UCC Sales Article.

Choice "Rescind the contract even if there was no reliance on the fraudulent…" (Incorrect): A party cannot charge fraud and use that as a basis to rescind the contract if they cannot prove that they justifiably relied on the other party's fraudulent misrepresentations.
questions.explanationJa: 契約成立時の詐欺が証明されれば、その契約を取り消すことができ、さらに詐欺によって生じた損害の賠償を求めて訴えることもできる。ただし、契約を取り消す場合、原告は相手方から受け取った対価を原則として返還しなければならない。UCC売買編では懲罰的損害賠償は認められていない。また、相手方の詐欺的な不実表示を正当に信頼したことを証明できなければ、詐欺を根拠に契約を取り消すことはできない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.15

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the requirements of the Sales Article of the UCC when a firm offer has been made without specifying a means of acceptance but provides that the offer will remain open for ten days?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The acceptance must be in writing and signed by the offeree.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The offer will remain open for three months despite the 10-day limitation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The acceptance can contain minor variations and still create an enforceable contract.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The offer can be from either a merchant or nonmerchant.

questions.explanation:
UCC Article 2 governs contracts for the sale of goods. Under Article 2, a firm offer is a term or condition to a sales contract that cannot be revoked even if there is no consideration (value given) from the offeree.

A firm offer is created when the following conditions (SUM) are met:

Signed: The offeror must specifically sign a written offer on the page containing the offer. The offeree does not need to sign it ("The acceptance must be in writing and signed by the offeree.").

Up to three months: The offer is enforceable for the time specified in the written offer. However, there is no requirement that a specific time must be given. If no time is specified, it is open for a reasonable time but no longer than three months ("The offer will remain open for three months despite the 10-day limita…").

Merchant: The offeror must be a merchant; the firm offer rule does not apply to nonmerchants ("The offer can be from either a merchant or nonmerchant.").

Formation of sales contracts follows common law: there must be an offer, acceptance, and consideration. However, there are minor differences between the UCC sales contract rules and common law. Under the UCC, parties can form an enforceable sales contract even if the acceptance contains minor variations (two-day delivery date change).
questions.explanationJa: UCC第2編の確定申込み（firm offer）は、被申込者からの対価がなくても撤回できない申込みであり、申込者が書面に署名し、申込者が商人であることを要する（非商人には適用されない）。署名が必要なのは申込者であって、被申込者の承諾が書面で署名されている必要はない。申込みは書面で定めた期間（本問では10日）有効であり、3か月となるのは期間の定めがない場合の上限である。また、UCCではコモンローと異なり、承諾に軽微な相違（配送日の変更など）が含まれていても、執行可能な売買契約が成立し得る。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.16

questions.stem: EG Door Co., a manufacturer of custom exterior doors, verbally contracted with Art Contractors to design and build a $2,000 custom door for a house that Art was restoring. After EG had completed substantial work on the door, Art advised EG that the house had been destroyed by fire and Art was cancelling the contract. EG finished the door and shipped it to Art. Art refused to accept delivery. Art contends that the contract cannot be enforced because it violated the Statute of Frauds by not being in writing. Under the Sales Article of the UCC, is Art's contention correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, because the contract was not in writing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes, because the contract cannot be fully performed due to the fire.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No, because the goods were specially manufactured for Art and cannot be resold in EG's regular course of business.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No, because the cancellation of the contract was not made in writing.

questions.explanation:
Under the Statute of Frauds (SOF) a contract for the sale of goods in the amount of $500 or more must be in writing. However, there are certain instances in which the SOF writing requirement does not apply even when the contract price is $500 or more ("Yes, because the contract was not in writing."). One instance is when the goods are specifically manufactured at the buyer's request.

This exception is in place to protect the seller. In this scenario, EG Door Co relied on Art Contractors' verbal commitment to pay for a custom door once it was completed and delivered. EG used labor and material to create a door that more than likely can't be used anywhere else. It would be unfair to EG to allow Art to use the SOF as a defense and not pay for the door.

However, if the door was a standard door that could be returned to EG's inventory and sold to another customer, then the SOF writing requirement would apply.

("Yes, because the contract cannot be fully performed due to the fire.") EG had substantially performed the contract at the time of Art's cancellation.

("No, because the cancellation of the contract was not made in writing.") Cancellation of a sale of goods contract is not required to be in writing.
questions.explanationJa: 詐欺防止法の下では、$500以上の物品売買契約は書面でなければならないが、価格が$500以上でも書面要件が適用されない例外がある。その一つが、買主の求めに応じて特別に製造された物品であり、売主の通常の営業過程で他に転売できない場合である。本問のEGは、Artの口頭の約束を信頼して、他では使えない可能性が高い$2,000の特注ドアの製作に労力と材料を費やしており、Artが詐欺防止法を盾に支払いを拒むのは不公平である。したがって、Artの主張は誤りである。なお、EGはArtの解除の時点で相当な作業を終えており、物品売買契約の解除は書面で行う必要もない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.17

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, when a contract for the sale of goods stipulates that the seller ship the goods by common carrier "F.O.B. purchaser's loading dock," which of the parties bears the risk of loss during shipment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The purchaser, because risk of loss passes when the goods are delivered to the carrier.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The purchaser, because title to the goods passes at the time of shipment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The seller, because risk of loss passes only when the goods reach the purchaser's loading dock.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The seller, because risk of loss remains with the seller until the goods are accepted by the purchaser.

questions.explanation: When goods are shipped under the terms "F.O.B. purchaser's loading dock", title and risk of loss generally pass to the purchaser, unless otherwise specified in the contract, only when the common carrier reaches the purchaser's loading dock with the goods.
questions.explanationJa: 「F.O.B. purchaser's loading dock（買主の荷受場渡し）」の条件で出荷された場合、契約に別段の定めがない限り、所有権と危険負担は運送人が物品を買主の荷受場に届けた時点で初めて買主に移転する。したがって、輸送中の危険は売主が負担する。運送人への引渡し時や出荷時に移転するのはFOB出荷地点の場合であり、また買主の承認時まで危険が売主にとどまるわけでもない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.18

questions.stem:
Under the Sales Article of the UCC, which of the following rights is (are) available to the buyer when a seller commits an anticipatory breach of contract?
Demand assurance of performance | Cancel the contract | Collect punitive damages

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | Yes | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes | No | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | Yes | Yes

questions.explanation:
Anticipatory breach of contract occurs when it doesn't appear that one party to a contract will perform the contract. At this point, the (wronged) party can request (demand) assurance of the other party's ability to perform the contract. If the other party fails or refuses to assure performance, the wronged party can cancel the contract and sue for damages.

For instance, a buyer orders goods from a seller. If the buyer anticipates the seller will not deliver the goods, the buyer can request assurance from the seller that the goods will be delivered. If the seller fails to give assurance, the buyer can cancel the contact and sue for damages (advertising costs promoting sale of the goods).

Damages for breach of contract are awarded solely to return the injured party to the same economic position it occupied before the breach. A punitive damage award would enrich the injured party beyond the economic position of the original transaction in the contract. Therefore, it is not appropriate for breach of contract. However, punitive damages are awarded in cases involving torts (bodily injury).
questions.explanationJa: 履行期前の契約違反は、相手方が契約を履行しないと見込まれる場合に生じる。被害を受ける当事者は、相手方に履行の保証を求めることができ、相手方が保証を拒んだり提供しなかったりすれば、契約を解除して損害賠償を請求できる。契約違反の損害賠償は、被害当事者を違反前と同じ経済的状態に戻すためだけに認められるものであり、それを超えて利得させる懲罰的損害賠償は契約違反には適切でない（懲罰的損害賠償は人身傷害などの不法行為で認められる）。したがって、買主は履行の保証の要求と契約の解除はできるが、懲罰的損害賠償は得られない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.19

questions.stem: Under the UCC Sales Article, an action for breach of the implied warranty of merchantability by a party who sustains personal injuries may be successful against the seller of the product only when

choices.label: A
choices.text: The seller is a merchant of the product involved.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An action based on negligence can also be successfully maintained.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The injured party is in privity of contract with the seller.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An action based on strict liability in tort can also be successfully maintained.

questions.explanation:
When goods are sold, the seller makes certain promises to the buyer that the buyer can legally enforce if needed. These promises are known as warranties and can be express or implied.

The warranty of merchantability (WOM) is an implied warranty that arises as a matter of law. In an action (lawsuit) for breach of the WOM, an injured party needs to prove all three of the following:

The goods purchased were not fit for the ordinary (normal) purpose intended and therefore caused an injury to the purchaser.

The seller was a merchant who ordinarily sells the goods purchased.

The seller did not disclaim the WOM.

A seller can disclaim the WOM by making a written or oral statement that specifically mentions "merchantability" in the disclaiming statement, or by selling the goods "as is" or "with all faults."

("An action based on negligence can also be successfully maintained." / "The injured party is in privity of contract with the seller." / "An action based on strict liability in tort can also be successfully…") It is not necessary to also prove negligence, privity of contract, or strict liability to prove a breach of the WOM.
questions.explanationJa: 商品性の保証（warranty of merchantability）は法律上当然に生じる黙示の保証である。その違反を理由とする訴訟では、購入した物品が通常の用途に適さずに損害を生じさせたこと、売主がその物品を通常販売する商人であること、売主が商品性の保証を放棄していないことを立証する必要がある。したがって、人身傷害を受けた者の請求が認められるのは、売主がその製品の商人である場合に限られる。過失、privity、不法行為上の厳格責任をあわせて立証する必要はない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.20

questions.stem: Which of the following contracts is governed by the Sales Article of the UCC

choices.label: A
choices.text: A sale of stock on the stock exchange.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Construction of a house by a professional builder.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A sale of a used car by a nonmerchant.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A sale of an acre of land by a real estate agent.

questions.explanation:
Article 2 of the UCC deals with contracts for the sale of goods. The seller of the goods may be a merchant or nonmerchant. A merchant deals in the goods involved in the transaction; a nonmerchant is a seller who does not regularly deal in the goods involved in the transaction. In this scenario, a used car is tangible personal property; therefore, its sale by a nonmerchant is covered by Article 2 of the UCC.

("A sale of stock on the stock exchange.") Article 2 specifically excludes investment securities (stock) from the definitions of "goods." Therefore, a contract for the sale of stock is not covered by Article 2. Contracts involving the sale of stock on an exchange are covered by other laws, such as Article 8 of the UCC and the Securities and Exchange Act of 1934.

("Construction of a house by a professional builder." / "A sale of an acre of land by a real estate agent.") Contracts involving real property (land sales) or services (house construction) are covered by common law, not Article 2.
questions.explanationJa: UCC第2編は物品の売買契約を扱い、売主は商人でも、その物品を通常扱わない非商人でもよい。中古車は有体動産なので、非商人による中古車の売却は第2編の対象となる。株式などの投資証券は第2編の「物品」の定義から明示的に除外されており、UCC第8編や証券取引所法など他の法律が適用される。不動産（土地の売却）や役務（住宅の建設）の契約はコモンローの対象であり、第2編は適用されない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.21

questions.stem: Under the UCC Sales Article, which of the following conditions will prevent the formation of an enforceable sale of goods requirements contract?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Open price.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Open delivery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Open quantity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Open acceptance.

questions.explanation:
Formation of sales contracts follows common law: to form a contract, there must be an offer, acceptance, and consideration. The contract has not yet been formed if the acceptance remains open.

There are some minor differences between the UCC sales contract rules and common law. Under the UCC, parties can form an enforceable requirements sales contract and leave the price, delivery terms, and quantity open. Those terms can be determined later based on reasonable standards or objective facts ("Open price." / "Open delivery." / "Open quantity.").

In a requirements contract, the seller agrees to supply all the goods the buyer needs for a specified product for a specific period. The buyer agrees to purchase whatever it needs entirely from that seller. The exact price and quantity are often left open because the parties don't know the exact amounts when the contract is formed.

For the quantity, it is enough to say "all the goods we need."

For the price, it is enough to agree that the price will be the current market price when shipped.

The delivery terms are left open to obtain the best available method at the time the goods are ready to ship.
questions.explanationJa: 売買契約の成立はコモンローと同様に申込み・承諾・約因を要するため、承諾が未定のままであれば契約はまだ成立していない。一方、UCCでは、価格・引渡条件・数量を未定のままにしても、執行可能な必要量供給契約（requirements contract）を成立させることができ、これらの条件は合理的な基準や客観的事実に基づいて後で決められる。必要量供給契約では、売主は一定期間買主が必要とする物品をすべて供給し、買主はそれをすべてその売主から購入することに合意する。数量は「必要な分すべて」、価格は「出荷時の時価」とすれば足り、引渡条件も出荷時点で最適な方法を選べるよう未定にできる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.22

questions.stem: Under the UCC Sales Article, which of the following legal remedies would a buyer not have when a seller fails to transfer and deliver goods identified to the contract?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Suit for specific performance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Suit for punitive damages.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Purchase substitute goods (cover).

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recover the identified goods (capture).

questions.explanation:
Choice "Suit for punitive damages." (Correct): Punitive damages, which are amounts of compensation in excess of a victim's actual loss, are not available under the UCC Sales Article. The buyer has the right to purchase substitute goods or, if that isn't possible, to exercise the right of replevin to capture the identified goods in exchange for paying the contract price to the seller.

Choice "Suit for specific performance." (Incorrect): When unique goods are involved, the buyer may be entitled to demand specific performance.

Choice "Purchase substitute goods (cover)." (Incorrect): The buyer has the right to purchase substitute goods

Choice "Recover the identified goods (capture)." (Incorrect): The buyer has the right of replevin to capture the identified goods in exchange for paying the contract price to the seller.
questions.explanationJa: 懲罰的損害賠償は被害者の実際の損失を超える賠償であり、UCC売買編では認められていない。したがって、売主が特定された物品を引き渡さない場合でも、買主は懲罰的損害賠償を求めて訴えることはできない。一方、買主は代替品を購入すること（cover）ができ、それが不可能な場合には、契約代金を支払うのと引き換えに特定された物品を取り戻すこと（replevin）ができる。また、唯一無二の物品が対象であれば、特定履行を求めることもできる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Sales Contracts Q.23

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, which of the following statements is correct regarding the creation of express warranties?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Express warranties must contain formal words such as warranty or guarantee.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Express warranties must be part of the basis of the bargain between buyer and seller.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Express warranties are not enforceable if made orally.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Express warranties cannot be based on statements made in the seller's promotional materials.

questions.explanation:
Under UCC §2-313, an express warranty is created by any affirmation of fact or promise, any description of the goods, or any sample or model that becomes part of the basis of the bargain. The statement must be part of the basis of the bargain between buyer and seller.

Formal words such as "warrant" or "guarantee" are not required; §2-313(2) states that no specific intention to make a warranty or formal wording is needed.
Express warranties may be made orally; there is no writing requirement for a warranty.
Statements in the seller's advertising or promotional materials can create express warranties if they become part of the basis of the bargain. Mere opinion or sales talk ("puffing"), however, does not.
questions.explanationJa:
UCC §2-313 により、明示の保証は、事実の表明・約束、物品の説明、見本・模型が「取引の基礎（basis of the bargain）」の一部となったときに成立する。
「保証する」等の形式的な文言は不要であり、口頭でも成立する。売主の広告・販促資料の記述も取引の基礎となれば明示の保証になる（単なる意見や誇張的な宣伝文句は除く）。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.6 (AICPA No. 9846)

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, which of the following requirements must be met for a writing to be an enforceable contract for the sale of goods?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The writing must contain a term specifying the price of the goods.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The writing must contain a term specifying the quantity of the goods.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The writing must contain the signatures of all parties to the writing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The writing must contain the signature of the party seeking to enforce the writing.

questions.explanation:
Under the UCC statute of frauds (§2-201(1)), a contract for the sale of goods for $500 or more requires a writing sufficient to indicate that a contract has been made, signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought. The writing is not insufficient because it omits or incorrectly states a term, but the contract is not enforceable beyond the quantity of goods shown in the writing. Quantity is therefore the one term that must be stated.

The price term may be omitted; the UCC supplies a reasonable price (§2-305).
Signatures of all parties are not required; only the party against whom enforcement is sought must have signed.
The signature of the party seeking enforcement is irrelevant; it is the defendant's signature that matters.
questions.explanationJa:
UCC §2-201(1)（詐欺防止法）により、$500 以上の物品売買契約は、契約の成立を示す書面で、履行を求められる側（被告側）が署名したものが必要。書面に条項の欠落や誤りがあっても有効だが、書面に記載された数量を超えては強制できないため、数量は必ず記載が要る。
価格は記載が無くても合理的な価格が補充される（§2-305）。全当事者の署名は不要で、強制される側の署名だけでよい。強制を求める側の署名は関係ない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.5 (AICPA No. 89805)

questions.stem: When do title and risk of loss for conforming goods pass to the buyer under a shipment contract covered by the Sales Article of the UCC?

choices.label: A
choices.text: When the goods are identified and designated for shipment

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the goods are given to a common carrier

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the goods arrive at their destination

choices.label: D
choices.text: When the goods are tendered to the buyer at their destination

questions.explanation:
Under a shipment contract, the seller is required only to deliver conforming goods to a carrier. Unless otherwise agreed, title passes when the seller completes physical delivery, which is when the goods are delivered to the carrier (UCC §2-401(2)(a)), and risk of loss passes to the buyer when the goods are duly delivered to the carrier (UCC §2-509(1)(a)).

Identification and designation of the goods gives the buyer a special property interest (§2-501) but does not pass title or risk of loss.
Arrival at the destination, or tender at the destination, is when title and risk pass under a destination contract, not a shipment contract.
questions.explanationJa:
出荷契約（shipment contract）では、売主は適合物品を運送人に引き渡せばよく、別段の合意が無い限り、所有権（UCC §2-401(2)(a)）も危険負担（§2-509(1)(a)）も運送人への引渡し時に買主へ移転する。
物品の特定は買主に特別な財産的利益を与えるだけで、所有権・危険負担は移らない。仕向地への到着や仕向地での提供の時点で移転するのは仕向地契約（destination contract）の場合である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.6 (AICPA No. 89806)

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, which of the following circumstances best describes how the implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose arises in a sale of goods transaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The buyer is purchasing the goods for a particular purpose and is relying on the seller’s skill or judgment to select suitable goods.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The buyer is purchasing the goods for a particular purpose and the seller is a merchant in such goods.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The seller knows the particular purpose for which the buyer will use the goods and knows the buyer is relying on the seller’s skill or judgment to select suitable goods.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The seller knows the particular purpose for which the buyer will use the goods and the seller is a merchant in such goods.

questions.explanation:
Under UCC §2-315, an implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose arises when the seller, at the time of contracting, has reason to know the particular purpose for which the goods are required and that the buyer is relying on the seller's skill or judgment to select or furnish suitable goods. Both elements focus on the seller's knowledge; the seller does not need to be a merchant.

The statement that the buyer is buying for a particular purpose and relying on the seller describes only the buyer's state of mind; the warranty requires that the seller know of the purpose and the reliance. The statements that require the seller to be a merchant describe the implied warranty of merchantability under UCC §2-314, not fitness for a particular purpose, and a merchant seller who knows the purpose but not the buyer's reliance does not give the fitness warranty.
questions.explanationJa:
UCC §2-315では、契約時に売主が①買主の特定の使用目的と②買主が売主の技能・判断に依拠して適切な物品を選ぶことを知っている（知るべき理由がある）ときに、特定目的適合性の黙示保証が生じる。要件は売主側の認識であり、売主が商人である必要はない。

「買主が特定目的で購入し売主に依拠している」だけでは買主側の事情にとどまり、売主の認識が欠ける。「売主が商人であること」を要件とする記述は§2-314の商品性の黙示保証の要件であり、目的を知っていても依拠を知らない商人には適合性保証は生じない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.3 (AICPA No. 90203)

questions.stem: On day 1, Jackson, a merchant, mailed Sands a signed letter that contained an offer to sell Sands 500 electric fans at $10 per fan. The letter was received by Sands on day 3. The letter contained a promise not to revoke the offer but no expiration date. On day 4, Jackson mailed Sands a revocation of the offer to sell the fans. Sands received the revocation on day 6. On day 7, Sands mailed Jackson an acceptance of the offer. Jackson received the acceptance on day 9. Under the Sales Article of the UCC, was a contract formed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No contract was formed because the offer failed to state an expiration date.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No contract was formed because Sands received the revocation of the offer before Sands accepted the offer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A contract was formed on the day Jackson received Sands’ acceptance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A contract was formed on the day Sands mailed the acceptance to Jackson.

questions.explanation:
Under UCC §2-205, a firm offer is an offer by a merchant to buy or sell goods in a signed writing that by its terms gives assurance it will be held open. It is irrevocable without consideration for the time stated or, if no time is stated, for a reasonable time not exceeding three months. Jackson, a merchant, made the offer in a signed letter promising not to revoke it, so the day-4 revocation was ineffective. Under UCC §2-206(1), an offer invites acceptance in any manner and by any medium reasonable in the circumstances; an acceptance sent by a reasonable medium such as mail is effective when dispatched (the mailbox rule). Sands' acceptance was therefore effective on day 7, when it was mailed.

The lack of an expiration date does not prevent a firm offer; the offer stays open for a reasonable time up to three months. Receipt of the revocation does not matter because a merchant's firm offer cannot be revoked during that period. The contract was formed on dispatch, not on day 9 when Jackson received the acceptance.
questions.explanationJa:
UCC §2-205の確定申込み（firm offer）は、商人が署名した書面で申込みを維持すると保証したもので、約因がなくても、期間の定めがあればその期間、なければ3か月を超えない合理的期間、撤回できない。商人であるJacksonは撤回しない旨を記した署名入り書面で申し込んでおり、4日目の撤回は無効。§2-206(1)により、申込みは状況に照らし合理的な方法・媒体での承諾を誘引し、郵便など合理的な媒体による承諾は発信時に効力を生じる（発信主義）。よってSandsが承諾を投函した7日目に契約が成立した。

期限の記載がなくても確定申込みは成立し、最長3か月の合理的期間有効である。撤回の通知を受領していても、商人の確定申込みはその期間中撤回できない。契約成立はJacksonが承諾を受領した9日目ではなく発信時である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.24 (AICPA No. 90224)

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, which of the following oral contracts for the sale of goods valued at more than $500 is most likely to be unenforceable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A contract to sell a work of art.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A contract to sell goods specially manufactured for the buyer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A contract to sell fuel oil, where the contract is admitted to in court.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A contract to sell furniture where half of the value of the shipment has been received and accepted.

questions.explanation:
Under the UCC statute of frauds, a contract for the sale of goods for $500 or more is not enforceable unless there is a writing signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought (UCC §2-201(1)). An oral contract to sell a work of art fits none of the exceptions in §2-201(3), so it is the contract most likely to be unenforceable.

Section 2-201(3) makes oral contracts enforceable for specially manufactured goods not suitable for sale to others once the seller has substantially begun manufacture or made commitments, when the party against whom enforcement is sought admits the contract in court (enforceable up to the quantity admitted), and for goods that have been received and accepted (enforceable to the extent of those goods, here half of the furniture shipment).
questions.explanationJa:
UCCの詐欺防止法（statute of frauds）により、$500以上の物品売買契約は、強制される側が署名した書面がなければ強制できない（UCC §2-201(1)）。美術品を売る口頭契約は§2-201(3)の例外のどれにも当たらないので、最も強制できない可能性が高い。

§2-201(3)では、他に転売できない特注品で売主が製造に実質的に着手した場合、強制される側が法廷で契約の存在を認めた場合（認めた数量まで）、物品が受領・受容された場合（その物品の範囲、本問では家具の半分）には、口頭契約でも強制できる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.19 (AICPA No. 59577)

questions.stem: Gold contracted in writing to sell Hatch a used computer for $150. Hatch went to Gold's home with the money but Gold refused to deliver the computer. What would be the nature of Hatch's remedy against Gold?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Specific performance only.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Compensatory damages only.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Specific performance and consequential damages only.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Punitive damages and compensatory damages only.

questions.explanation:
A used computer is a good, so UCC Article 2 governs. When a seller fails to deliver, the buyer may recover compensatory damages, such as the difference between the market price and the contract price (UCC §2-713) or the cost of cover (UCC §2-712). Specific performance is available only when the goods are unique or in other proper circumstances (UCC §2-716); an ordinary used computer is readily available elsewhere, so specific performance is not appropriate.

Specific performance alone, or specific performance with consequential damages, is not available because the computer is not unique. Punitive damages are not awarded for a mere breach of contract, so punitive damages with compensatory damages is incorrect.
questions.explanationJa:
中古パソコンは物品なので UCC 第2編が適用される。売主が引渡しを拒んだ場合、買主は市場価格と契約価格の差額（UCC §2-713）や代替品購入費用（UCC §2-712）などの填補賠償（compensatory damages）を請求できる。特定履行は物品が唯一無二である場合など適切な状況に限られ（UCC §2-716）、一般的な中古パソコンは他で入手できるため認められない。

物品が唯一無二ではないので、特定履行のみ、または特定履行と結果的損害の組合せは認められない。単なる契約違反に懲罰的損害賠償は認められないため、懲罰的損害と填補賠償の組合せも誤り。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.5 (AICPA No. 57601)

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, a firm offer will be created only if the

choices.label: A
choices.text: Offer states the time period during which it will remain open.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Offer is made by a merchant in a signed writing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Offeree gives some form of consideration.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Offeree is a merchant.

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-205, a firm offer arises when a merchant makes an offer to buy or sell goods in a signed writing that by its terms gives assurance it will be held open. Such an offer is irrevocable for the time stated, or for a reasonable time if none is stated, but in no event longer than three months. The requirement that the offer state the time period during which it will remain open is incorrect because, if no period is stated, the offer is held open for a reasonable time (up to three months). The requirement that the offeree give some form of consideration is incorrect because a firm offer is binding without consideration; that is the key difference from a common-law option contract. The requirement that the offeree be a merchant is incorrect because only the offeror must be a merchant.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-205 のファーム・オファー（撤回できない申込み）は、商人である申込者が、申込みを一定期間維持すると約束した署名付きの書面で申し込んだときに成立する。期間の定めがあればその期間、定めがなければ合理的な期間、撤回できない（いずれも最長3か月）。期間の明示は要件ではない（定めがなければ合理的期間となる）。被申込者の約因も不要で、これがコモンローのオプション契約との違いである。商人であることが求められるのは申込者だけで、被申込者は商人でなくてよい。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.1

questions.stem:
Under the Sales Article of the UCC, when a written offer has been made without specifying a means of acceptance but providing that the offer will only remain open for ten days, which of the following statements represent(s) a valid acceptance of the offer?

I. An acceptance sent by regular mail the day before the ten-day period expires that reaches the offeror on the eleventh day.
II. An acceptance faxed the day before the ten-day period expires that reaches the offeror on the eleventh day, due to a malfunction of the offeror's printer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: I only

choices.label: B
choices.text: II only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both I and II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither I nor II

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-206(1)(a), unless the offer unambiguously indicates otherwise, an offer invites acceptance in any manner and by any medium reasonable in the circumstances. Because this offer did not specify a means of acceptance or require that the acceptance be received by the deadline, the mailbox (deposited acceptance) rule applies: an acceptance sent by a reasonable medium is effective when dispatched, not when received. Statement I is a valid acceptance because the mailed acceptance was sent within the ten-day period, even though it reached the offeror on the eleventh day. Statement II is also a valid acceptance because fax is a reasonable medium and the acceptance was sent within the ten-day period; the late arrival caused by the offeror's own printer does not affect the time of acceptance. Therefore neither 'I only' nor 'II only' is complete, and 'Neither I nor II' wrongly treats receipt as the time of acceptance.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-206(1)(a) により、申込みが明確に限定していない限り、状況に照らして合理的な方法・媒体で承諾できる。本問の申込みは承諾方法を指定しておらず、期限内の到達も求めていないので、発信主義（メールボックス・ルール）が適用され、合理的な媒体による承諾は発信した時点で効力を生じる。Iの郵便による承諾は10日以内に発送されているので、到達が11日目でも有効である。IIのファックスも合理的な媒体で期限内に送信されており、到達の遅れは申込者自身のプリンターの故障によるものなので、承諾の効力に影響しない。したがって両方とも有効な承諾であり、到達時点を基準にする考え方は誤りである。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.2

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, the warranty of title

choices.label: A
choices.text: Provides that the seller cannot disclaim the warranty if the sale is made to a bona fide purchaser for value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Provides that the seller deliver the goods free from any lien of which the buyer lacked knowledge when the contract was made.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Applies only if it is in writing and signed by the seller.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Applies only if the seller is a merchant.

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-312(1), every contract for sale contains a warranty by the seller that the title conveyed is good, its transfer rightful, and the goods will be delivered free from any security interest or other lien or encumbrance of which the buyer at the time of contracting has no knowledge. The statement that the seller cannot disclaim the warranty for a bona fide purchaser is incorrect because §2-312(2) allows the warranty of title to be excluded or modified by specific language or by circumstances giving the buyer reason to know the seller does not claim full title. The statement that the warranty applies only if it is in writing and signed is incorrect because the warranty arises automatically by operation of law. The statement that it applies only to merchant sellers is incorrect because the warranty of title is given by every seller; only the additional warranty against infringement in §2-312(3) is limited to merchants.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-312(1) により、すべての売買契約には、売主が移転する権原が正当であり、買主が契約時に知らなかった担保権その他の負担のない状態で物品を引き渡すという権原の保証が含まれる。権原の保証は、特定の文言や、売主が完全な権原を主張していないと買主が知りうる状況があれば排除・修正できるので（§2-312(2)）、善意の有償取得者への売買なら排除できないという記述は誤り。この保証は法律上当然に生じるので、書面や署名は要らない。また、権原の保証はすべての売主が負うもので、商人に限られるのは§2-312(3)の権利侵害がないことの保証だけである。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.3

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, which of the following factors is most important in determining who bears the risk of loss in a sale of goods contract?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The method of shipping the goods.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The contract's shipping terms.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Title to the goods.

choices.label: D
choices.text: How the goods were lost.

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-509, when there is no breach, risk of loss is allocated first by the parties' agreement and, in shipment situations, by the contract's shipping terms: in a shipment contract (e.g., F.O.B. seller's place) risk passes when the goods are duly delivered to the carrier, and in a destination contract (e.g., F.O.B. buyer's place) risk passes when the goods are tendered at the destination. The method of shipping the goods (truck, rail, air) does not itself determine who bears the risk. Title to the goods is not controlling because the UCC allocates risk of loss independently of title. How the goods were lost is irrelevant to the allocation of risk; it matters only to whether insurance or a carrier claim covers the loss.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-509 では、契約違反がない場合、損失の危険は当事者の合意、そして運送を伴う場合は契約の出荷条件で決まる。出荷地契約（F.O.B. 売主側の地点）なら運送人への引渡し時に、仕向地契約（F.O.B. 買主側の地点）なら仕向地での提供時に危険が買主へ移る。トラックや鉄道といった輸送方法そのものは危険負担を決めない。UCCは危険負担を権原（所有権）と切り離して定めるので、権原の所在も決め手にならない。物品がどのように失われたかも、危険の帰属とは関係がない。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.5

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, in an F.O.B. place of shipment contract, the risk of loss passes to the buyer when the goods

choices.label: A
choices.text: Are identified to the contract.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Are placed on the seller's loading dock.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Are delivered to the carrier.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reach the buyer's loading dock.

questions.explanation: An F.O.B. place of shipment term creates a shipment contract (UCC §2-319(1)(a)). Under UCC §2-509(1)(a), when the contract requires or authorizes the seller to ship the goods by carrier but does not require delivery at a particular destination, risk of loss passes to the buyer when the goods are duly delivered to the carrier. Identification of the goods to the contract gives the buyer a special property and insurable interest (§2-501) but does not shift risk of loss. Placing the goods on the seller's loading dock is not enough because the goods must actually be delivered to the carrier. Reaching the buyer's loading dock describes when risk passes in a destination contract, not a shipment contract.
questions.explanationJa: F.O.B. 出荷地条件は出荷地契約である（UCC §2-319(1)(a)）。§2-509(1)(a) により、売主が運送人による発送を求められ、特定の仕向地での引渡しまでは求められていない場合、物品が運送人に適切に引き渡された時点で損失の危険が買主に移る。物品の特定は買主に特別財産権・被保険利益を与えるだけで（§2-501）、危険は移らない。売主の荷積み場に置いただけでは運送人への引渡しにならない。買主の荷積み場への到着で危険が移るのは仕向地契約の場合である。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.6

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, and unless otherwise agreed to, the seller's obligation to the buyer is to

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deliver the goods to the buyer's place of business.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hold conforming goods and give the buyer whatever notification is reasonably necessary to enable the buyer to take delivery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deliver all goods called for in the contract to a common carrier.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set aside conforming goods for inspection by the buyer before delivery.

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-503(1), tender of delivery requires the seller to put and hold conforming goods at the buyer's disposition and give the buyer any notification reasonably necessary to enable the buyer to take delivery. Unless otherwise agreed, the place for delivery is the seller's place of business (or residence if none) under §2-308(a). Delivering the goods to the buyer's place of business is not required because, absent agreement, the place of delivery is the seller's place of business. Delivering all goods to a common carrier is required only when the contract requires or authorizes shipment by carrier (§2-504). Setting aside conforming goods for inspection before delivery is not the seller's basic obligation; the buyer's inspection right (§2-513) is exercised on tender or delivery, not through a separate set-aside duty.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-503(1) の引渡しの提供では、売主は契約に適合する物品を買主が自由に処分できる状態に置いて保持し、買主が引き取るために合理的に必要な通知をすればよい。別段の合意がなければ、引渡し場所は売主の営業所である（§2-308(a)）。したがって買主の営業所まで届ける義務はない。運送人に引き渡す義務は、契約が運送人による発送を求めるか認める場合に限られる（§2-504）。検査のために物品を取り分けておくことも売主の基本的な義務ではなく、買主の検査権（§2-513）は引渡しの提供や引渡しの際に行使されるものである。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.7

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, which of the following statements is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The obligations of the parties to the contract must be performed in good faith.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Merchants and nonmerchants are treated alike.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The contract must involve the sale of goods for a price of more than $500.

choices.label: D
choices.text: None of the provisions of the UCC may be disclaimed by agreement.

questions.explanation: UCC §1-304 imposes an obligation of good faith in the performance and enforcement of every contract or duty within the UCC, so the parties to a sales contract must perform their obligations in good faith. The statement that merchants and nonmerchants are treated alike is incorrect because Article 2 contains special rules for merchants, such as the firm offer rule (§2-205), the merchant's confirmation rule (§2-201(2)), and the implied warranty of merchantability (§2-314). The statement that the contract must involve goods priced over $500 is incorrect because Article 2 applies to transactions in goods regardless of price (§2-102); the $500 figure matters only for the Statute of Frauds. The statement that no provision may be disclaimed is incorrect because, under §1-302, the effect of most UCC provisions may be varied by agreement, except duties such as good faith, diligence, reasonableness, and care.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §1-304 は、UCCの対象となるすべての契約・義務の履行と行使に信義誠実の義務を課しているので、売買契約の当事者は誠実に履行しなければならない。第2編にはファーム・オファー（§2-205）、商人間の確認書（§2-201(2)）、商品性の黙示保証（§2-314）など商人だけに適用される規定があるので、商人と非商人が同じに扱われるわけではない。第2編は価格に関係なく物品の取引に適用され（§2-102）、$500 は詐欺防止法の基準にすぎない。また §1-302 により、信義誠実・注意などの義務を除き、UCCの規定の多くは合意で変更できる。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.8

questions.stem: Under the Sales Article of the UCC, which of the following statements is correct regarding the warranty of merchantability arising when there has been a sale of goods by a merchant seller?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The warranty must be in writing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The warranty arises when the buyer relies on the seller's skill in selecting the goods purchased.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The warranty cannot be disclaimed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The warranty arises as a matter of law when the seller ordinarily sells the goods purchased.

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-314(1), unless excluded or modified, a warranty that the goods are merchantable is implied in a contract for their sale if the seller is a merchant with respect to goods of that kind. Because it is implied, it arises by operation of law whenever the seller ordinarily deals in the goods sold. The statement that the warranty must be in writing is incorrect because an implied warranty requires no writing at all. The statement that it arises when the buyer relies on the seller's skill in selecting the goods describes the implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose (§2-315), not merchantability. The statement that it cannot be disclaimed is incorrect because §2-316(2) and (3) allow disclaimer by language mentioning merchantability (conspicuous if in writing) or by expressions such as 'as is' or 'with all faults.'
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-314(1) により、売主がその種類の物品を扱う商人であれば、排除・修正されない限り、売買契約には物品が商品性を有するという保証が黙示的に含まれる。黙示の保証なので、売主がその物品を通常販売している限り、法律上当然に生じる。書面は要らない。買主が売主の選定の技量に依拠したときに生じるのは、特定目的適合性の黙示保証（§2-315）である。商品性の保証も、merchantability に言及する文言（書面なら目立つ表示）や 'as is'・'with all faults' などの表現で排除できる（§2-316(2)(3)）。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.9

questions.stem:
Under the Sales Article of the UCC, which of the following events will result in the risk of loss passing from a merchant seller to a buyer?

Tender at seller's place of business | Use of seller's truck to deliver

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: No | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | No

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-509(3), when the goods are not to be shipped by carrier and are not held by a bailee, risk of loss passes to the buyer on the buyer's receipt of the goods if the seller is a merchant; otherwise it passes on tender of delivery. Because the seller is a merchant, tender of the goods at the seller's place of business does not pass the risk; the buyer must actually take physical possession. Use of the seller's own truck to deliver does not pass the risk either, because the seller's truck is not an independent carrier, so the risk stays with the merchant seller until the buyer receives the goods. Therefore neither event passes the risk of loss to the buyer.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-509(3) により、運送人による発送も受寄者の保管もない場合、売主が商人なら買主が物品を受領した時点で、商人でなければ引渡しの提供の時点で損失の危険が買主に移る。本問の売主は商人なので、売主の営業所で引渡しを提供しただけでは危険は移らず、買主が現実に物品を受け取る必要がある。売主自身のトラックは独立した運送人ではないので、それで配送しても運送人への引渡しにはならず、買主が受領するまで危険は売主に残る。したがって、どちらの事象も危険を移転させない。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.11

questions.stem: Rowe Corp. purchased goods from Stair Co. that were shipped C.O.D. Under the Sales Article of the UCC, which of the following rights does Rowe have?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The right to inspect the goods before paying.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The right to possession of the goods before paying.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The right to reject nonconforming goods.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The right to delay payment for a reasonable period of time.

questions.explanation: When goods are shipped C.O.D. (collect on delivery), the buyer must pay before inspecting or taking the goods (UCC §2-513(3)(a)). However, under §2-512(2), payment required before inspection does not constitute an acceptance of the goods or impair the buyer's right to inspect afterward or any of its remedies, so Rowe may still reject goods that turn out to be nonconforming (§2-601). The right to inspect before paying is incorrect because the C.O.D. term removes that right. The right to possession before paying is incorrect because the carrier releases the goods only on payment. The right to delay payment for a reasonable period is incorrect because payment is due on delivery under a C.O.D. term.
questions.explanationJa: C.O.D.（代金引換）で発送された場合、買主は物品を検査・受領する前に代金を支払わなければならない（UCC §2-513(3)(a)）。ただし §2-512(2) により、検査前の支払いは物品の受領（acceptance）とはみなされず、支払後の検査権や救済も失われないので、Roweは不適合な物品を拒絶できる（§2-601）。C.O.D.条件では支払前の検査権はなく、運送人は支払いと引換えにしか物品を渡さないので、支払前に占有する権利もない。代金は引渡し時に支払うので、合理的期間の支払猶予も認められない。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.12

questions.stem: Under the UCC Sales Article, which of the following statements is correct concerning a contract involving a merchant seller and a non-merchant buyer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whether the UCC Sales Article is applicable does not depend on the price of the goods involved.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only the seller is obligated to perform the contract in good faith.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The contract will be either a sale or return or sale on approval contract.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The contract may not involve the sale of personal property with a price of more than $500.

questions.explanation: UCC §2-102 makes Article 2 applicable to transactions in goods; its application does not depend on the price of the goods or on whether the parties are merchants. Price matters only for particular rules, such as the $500 threshold of the Statute of Frauds (§2-201). The statement that only the seller must act in good faith is incorrect because §1-304 imposes the duty of good faith on every party to a contract within the UCC. The statement that the contract will be a sale or return or sale on approval is incorrect because those arrangements arise only when the parties agree that delivered goods may be returned even though they conform (§2-326). The statement that the contract may not involve personal property priced over $500 is incorrect because Article 2 covers goods at any price.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-102 により、第2編は物品の取引に適用され、価格や当事者が商人かどうかで適用が左右されることはない。価格が問題になるのは詐欺防止法の$500基準（§2-201）のような個別の規定だけである。信義誠実の義務は §1-304 によりすべての当事者に課されるので、売主だけが負うわけではない。sale or return や sale on approval は、適合品でも返品できると当事者が合意した場合に限って成立する（§2-326）。また、$500を超える動産の売買も第2編の対象になる。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.13
