questions.stem: Vick bought a used boat from Ocean Marina that disclaimed "any and all warranties" in connection with the sale. Ocean was unaware the boat had been stolen from Kidd. Vick surrendered it to Kidd when confronted with proof of the theft. Vick sued Ocean. Who is likely to prevail and why?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Vick, because the implied warranty of title has been breached.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Vick, because a merchant cannot disclaim implied warranties.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ocean, because of the disclaimer of warranties.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ocean, because Vick surrendered the boat to Kidd.

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-312(1), every seller warrants that the title conveyed is good and its transfer rightful. A thief acquires no title to stolen goods, so neither Ocean nor Vick obtained title, and Ocean breached the warranty of title even though it was unaware of the theft. Under §2-312(2), the warranty of title can be excluded only by specific language or by circumstances giving the buyer reason to know the seller does not claim full title; a general disclaimer of 'any and all warranties' is not enough. The claim that a merchant cannot disclaim implied warranties is incorrect because merchants may disclaim implied warranties by following §2-316. Ocean cannot rely on the general disclaimer for the reason above. Vick's surrender of the boat to its true owner does not defeat the claim; it is the very loss caused by the defective title.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-312(1) により、すべての売主は移転する権原が正当であることを保証する。盗人は盗品について権原を取得しないので、OceanもVickも権原を得ておらず、Oceanは盗難を知らなかったとしても権原の保証に違反している。権原の保証は、特定の文言か、売主が完全な権原を主張していないと買主が知りうる状況によってしか排除できず（§2-312(2)）、「一切の保証」を否認する一般的な文言では排除されない。商人でも §2-316 に従えば黙示保証を排除できるので、商人は黙示保証を排除できないという理由は誤り。真の所有者に船を引き渡したことは、権原の欠陥による損害そのものであり、請求を妨げない。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.14

questions.stem: Larch Corp. manufactured and sold Oak a stove. The sale documents included a disclaimer of warranty for personal injury. The stove was defective. It exploded causing serious injuries to Oak's spouse. Larch was notified one week after the explosion. Under the UCC Sales Article, which of the following statements concerning Larch's liability for personal injury to Oak's spouse would be correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Larch cannot be liable because of a lack of privity with Oak's spouse.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Larch will not be liable because of a failure to give proper notice.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Larch will be liable because the disclaimer was not a disclaimer of all liability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Larch will be liable because liability for personal injury cannot be disclaimed.

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-719(3), a limitation of consequential damages for injury to the person in the case of consumer goods is prima facie unconscionable, so a seller cannot effectively avoid liability for personal injury caused by defective goods sold to a consumer; the stove was sold to Oak and injured Oak's spouse, so Larch remains liable despite the disclaimer. Lack of privity is not a defense because §2-318 extends the seller's warranties to members of the buyer's family or household who may reasonably be expected to use the goods and are injured by a breach. Failure to give proper notice is not a defense because §2-607(3)(a) requires notice within a reasonable time after discovery of the breach, and notice one week after the explosion is reasonable. The statement that Larch is liable because the disclaimer was not a disclaimer of all liability gives the wrong reason; liability exists because a personal injury exclusion is ineffective, not because the disclaimer was too narrow.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-719(3) により、消費者向け物品について身体傷害による結果損害の責任を制限する条項は、一応非良心的（prima facie unconscionable）とされる。Oakに売られたストーブの欠陥でOakの配偶者が負傷した本問では、人身損害の責任を免責条項で免れることはできないので、Larchは責任を負う。§2-318 は売主の保証を、物品の使用が合理的に予想される買主の家族・同居者にも及ぼすので、直接の契約関係（privity）がないことは抗弁にならない。通知は違反の発見後合理的期間内にすればよく（§2-607(3)(a)）、爆発の1週間後の通知は合理的である。免責条項が全責任の免責でなかったから責任を負うという理由は誤りで、人身損害の免責そのものが無効だから責任を負うのである。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.15

questions.stem: Quick Corp. agreed to purchase 200 typewriters from Union Suppliers, Inc. Union is a wholesaler of appliances and Quick is an appliance retailer. The contract required Union to ship the typewriters to Quick by common carrier, "F.O.B. Union Suppliers, Inc. Loading Dock." Which of the parties bears the risk of loss during shipment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Union, because the risk of loss passes only when Quick receives the typewriters.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Union, because both parties are merchants.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Quick, because title to the typewriters passed to Quick at the time of shipment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Quick, because the risk of loss passes when the typewriters are delivered to the carrier.

questions.explanation: "F.O.B. Union Suppliers, Inc. Loading Dock" names the seller's place of shipment, so the contract is a shipment contract (UCC §2-319(1)(a)). Under §2-509(1)(a), in a shipment contract risk of loss passes to the buyer when the goods are duly delivered to the carrier, so Quick bears the risk during shipment. The claim that risk passes only when Quick receives the typewriters is incorrect; that rule (§2-509(3)) applies only when goods are not shipped by carrier. The fact that both parties are merchants does not keep the risk with Union, because the shipping terms control. The claim that Quick bears the risk because title passed at shipment gives the wrong reason; under the UCC, risk of loss is allocated by the contract's terms and §2-509, not by the location of title.
questions.explanationJa: 「F.O.B. Union Suppliers, Inc. Loading Dock」は売主側の出荷地を示すので出荷地契約である（UCC §2-319(1)(a)）。§2-509(1)(a) により、出荷地契約では物品が運送人に適切に引き渡された時点で損失の危険が買主に移るので、輸送中の危険はQuickが負う。Quickの受領時に危険が移るというのは、運送人による発送がない場合のルール（§2-509(3)）であり本問には当たらない。両当事者が商人であっても、出荷条件が優先するので危険はUnionに残らない。権原が出荷時に移ったからという理由も誤りで、UCCは危険負担を権原の所在とは切り離して定めている。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.16

questions.stem: Webstar Corp. orally agreed to sell Northco, Inc. a computer for $20,000. Northco sent a signed purchase order to Webstar confirming the agreement. Webstar received the purchase order and did not respond. Webstar refused to deliver the computer to Northco, claiming that the purchase order did not satisfy the UCC Statute of Frauds because it was not signed by Webstar. Northco sells computers to the general public and Webstar is a computer wholesaler. Under the UCC Sales Article, Webstar's position is

choices.label: A
choices.text: Incorrect, because it failed to object to Northco's purchase order.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Incorrect, because only the buyer in a sale-of-goods transaction must sign the contract.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Correct, because it was the party against whom enforcement of the contract is being sought.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Correct, because the purchase price of the computer exceeded $500.

questions.explanation: A contract for the sale of goods for $500 or more must ordinarily be evidenced by a writing signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought (UCC §2-201(1)). Under the merchant's confirmation rule in §2-201(2), however, between merchants, a written confirmation sent within a reasonable time that is sufficient against the sender satisfies the Statute of Frauds against the recipient, if the recipient has reason to know its contents and does not give written notice of objection within ten days after receiving it. Northco and Webstar both deal in computers and are merchants, and Webstar received Northco's signed confirmation and did not respond, so Webstar's failure to object makes its position incorrect. The statement that only the buyer must sign is incorrect because the Statute of Frauds focuses on the party against whom enforcement is sought, whether buyer or seller. Being the party against whom enforcement is sought does not help Webstar, because the merchant's confirmation substitutes for its signature. The price exceeding $500 only triggers the Statute of Frauds; it does not make Webstar's position correct when the confirmation rule is satisfied.
questions.explanationJa: $500以上の物品売買契約は、原則として履行を求められる側が署名した書面が必要である（UCC §2-201(1)）。ただし商人間では、合理的期間内に送られ送付者に対して有効な確認書を受け取った側が、内容を知りうる状態で受領後10日以内に書面で異議を述べなければ、受領者に対しても詐欺防止法の要件を満たす（§2-201(2)、商人間の確認書ルール）。NorthcoとWebstarはともにコンピュータを扱う商人で、Webstarは署名付きの注文書を受け取りながら異議を述べていないので、Webstarの主張は誤りである。署名が必要なのは買主に限らず履行を求められる側であり、買主だけが署名すればよいわけではない。Webstarが履行を求められる側であることは、確認書ルールが署名に代わるので主張の根拠にならない。価格が$500を超えることは詐欺防止法の適用の前提にすぎず、確認書ルールを満たしている以上、Webstarの主張を正当化しない。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.17

questions.stem: Which of the following statements applies to a sale on approval under the UCC Sales Article?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both the buyer and seller must be merchants.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The buyer must be purchasing the goods for resale.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Risk of loss for the goods passes to the buyer when the goods are accepted after the trial period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Title to the goods passes to the buyer on delivery of the goods to the buyer.

questions.explanation: A sale on approval is a transaction in which delivered goods may be returned even though they conform, and the goods are delivered primarily for the buyer's use (UCC §2-326(1)(a)). Under §2-327(1)(a), unless otherwise agreed, risk of loss and title do not pass to the buyer until the buyer accepts the goods; trial use alone is not acceptance. The statement that both parties must be merchants is incorrect because a sale on approval does not require merchant status. The statement that the buyer must purchase for resale is incorrect because goods delivered primarily for resale make the transaction a sale or return, not a sale on approval. The statement that title passes on delivery is incorrect because title, like risk of loss, remains with the seller until acceptance.
questions.explanationJa: sale on approval（試用売買）は、適合品でも返品でき、物品が主として買主の使用のために引き渡される取引である（UCC §2-326(1)(a)）。§2-327(1)(a) により、別段の合意がなければ、損失の危険も権原も買主が承認（受領）するまで移らず、試用しただけでは承認にならない。当事者が商人である必要はない。主として転売目的で引き渡される場合は sale or return であり、試用売買ではない。権原も危険と同じく承認まで売主に残るので、引渡し時に移るわけではない。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.18

questions.stem: Which of the following statements would not apply to a written contract governed by the provisions of the UCC Sales Article?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The contract may involve the sale of personal property.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The obligations of a nonmerchant may be different from those of a merchant.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The obligations of the parties must be performed in good faith.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The contract must involve the sale of goods for a price of $500 or more.

questions.explanation: Article 2 applies to transactions in goods regardless of price (UCC §2-102). The $500 figure relates only to the Statute of Frauds (§2-201), which determines when a writing is required; it is not a condition for Article 2 to govern a contract. Therefore the statement that the contract must involve goods priced at $500 or more does not apply. The other statements do apply: goods are tangible, movable personal property (§2-105), so the contract may involve the sale of personal property; Article 2 imposes special duties on merchants (for example §2-205 and §2-314), so a nonmerchant's obligations may differ from a merchant's; and §1-304 requires every contract within the UCC to be performed in good faith.
questions.explanationJa: 第2編は価格に関係なく物品の取引に適用される（UCC §2-102）。$500 は書面が必要かどうかを決める詐欺防止法（§2-201）の基準にすぎず、第2編が適用される条件ではない。したがって、$500以上の物品売買でなければならないという記述は当てはまらない。そのほかの記述は当てはまる。物品は有体の動産なので動産の売買を含みうる（§2-105）。第2編には商人だけに課される義務（§2-205、§2-314など）があるので、非商人の義務は商人と異なりうる。§1-304 により、UCCの契約はすべて誠実に履行しなければならない。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.19

questions.stem: Bond purchased a painting from Wool, who is not in the business of selling art. Wool tendered delivery of the painting after receiving payment in full from Bond. Bond informed Wool that Bond would be unable to take possession of the painting until later that day. Thieves stole the painting before Bond returned. The risk of loss

choices.label: A
choices.text: Passed to Bond at Wool's tender of delivery.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Passed to Bond at the time the contract was formed and payment was made.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remained with Wool, because the parties agreed on a later time of delivery.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Remained with Wool, because Bond had not yet received the painting.

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-509(3), when the goods are not shipped by carrier and are not held by a bailee, risk of loss passes to the buyer on receipt of the goods if the seller is a merchant; otherwise it passes on tender of delivery. Wool is not in the business of selling art, so Wool is a nonmerchant seller and the risk passed to Bond when Wool tendered delivery. Formation of the contract and payment do not themselves shift risk of loss, because the UCC ties risk to tender or receipt, not to payment. There was no agreement on a later delivery time; Wool tendered delivery and Bond merely chose not to take possession until later, so the risk did not remain with Wool on that basis. Receipt by the buyer is the test only for merchant sellers, so Bond's not yet having received the painting does not keep the risk with Wool.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-509(3) により、運送人による発送も受寄者の保管もない場合、売主が商人なら買主の受領時、商人でなければ引渡しの提供の時に損失の危険が買主に移る。Woolは美術品の販売を業としない非商人なので、Woolが引渡しを提供した時点で危険はBondに移った。契約の成立や代金の支払いそのものでは危険は移らない。後の引渡し時期を合意したわけではなく、Woolが引渡しを提供したのに対しBondが後で取りに来ると伝えただけなので、それを理由に危険がWoolに残ることはない。買主の受領を基準にするのは商人の売主の場合だけである。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.21

questions.stem: Smith contracted in writing to sell Peters a used personal computer for $600. The contract did not specifically address the time for payment, place of delivery, or Peters' right to inspect the computer. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Smith is obligated to deliver the computer to Peters' home.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Peters is entitled to inspect the computer before paying for it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Peters may not pay for the computer using a personal check unless Smith agrees.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Smith is not entitled to payment until 30 days after Peters receives the computer.

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-513(1), unless otherwise agreed, the buyer has a right before payment or acceptance to inspect the goods at any reasonable place and time and in any reasonable manner, so Peters may inspect the computer before paying. The claim that Smith must deliver to Peters' home is incorrect because, absent agreement, the place for delivery is the seller's place of business or, if none, the seller's residence (§2-308(a)). The claim that Peters may not pay by personal check without Smith's agreement is incorrect because tender of payment is sufficient when made by any means or in any manner current in the ordinary course of business, unless the seller demands legal tender and gives a reasonable extension of time to obtain it (§2-511(2)). The claim that payment is not due until 30 days after receipt is incorrect because, unless otherwise agreed, payment is due at the time and place at which the buyer is to receive the goods (§2-310(a)).
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-513(1) により、別段の合意がなければ、買主は支払いや受領の前に、合理的な場所・時期・方法で物品を検査する権利をもつので、Petersは代金を払う前にコンピュータを検査できる。合意がなければ引渡し場所は売主の営業所（なければ住所）なので（§2-308(a)）、Petersの自宅まで届ける義務はない。支払いは通常の取引で通用する方法であれば足り、売主が法定通貨を要求する場合も入手のための合理的な猶予を与えなければならないので（§2-511(2)）、個人小切手での支払いに売主の同意は要らない。代金は別段の合意がなければ買主が物品を受け取る時と場所で支払うもので（§2-310(a)）、受領後30日の猶予はない。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.22

questions.stem: On May 2, Lace Corp., an appliance wholesaler, offered to sell appliances worth $3,000 to Parco, Inc., a household appliances retailer. The offer was signed by Lace's president, and provided that it would not be withdrawn before June 1. It also included the shipping terms: "FOB - Parco's warehouse." On May 29, Parco mailed an acceptance of Lace's offer. Lace received the acceptance June 2. Which of the following statements is correct if Lace sent Parco a telegram revoking its offer, and Parco received the telegram on May 25?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A contract was formed on May 2.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lace's revocation effectively terminated its offer on May 25.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lace's revocation was ineffective because the offer could not be revoked before June 1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No contract was formed because Lace received Parco's acceptance after June 1.

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-205, an offer by a merchant to buy or sell goods in a signed writing that gives assurance it will be held open is irrevocable, without consideration, for the period stated (not exceeding three months). Lace, an appliance wholesaler, is a merchant, and its signed offer promised not to withdraw before June 1, so the May 25 revocation was ineffective. The statement that a contract was formed on May 2 is incorrect because only the offer was made on May 2; no contract exists until acceptance. The statement that the revocation terminated the offer on May 25 is incorrect because a firm offer cannot be revoked during its stated period. The statement that no contract was formed because the acceptance arrived after June 1 is incorrect because the offer did not require receipt by a deadline, so the acceptance mailed on May 29 was effective when dispatched (§2-206(1)(a)), within the period the offer was open.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-205 により、商人が署名付きの書面で一定期間申込みを維持すると約束した場合、約因がなくてもその期間（最長3か月）は撤回できない。家電卸売業者のLaceは商人であり、署名付きの申込みで6月1日まで撤回しないと約束しているので、5月25日に到達した撤回は効力がない。5月2日になされたのは申込みだけで、承諾があるまで契約は成立しない。ファーム・オファーは期間中撤回できないので、5月25日に申込みが消滅したわけでもない。申込みは期限内の到達を求めていないので、5月29日に郵送した承諾は発信時に効力を生じ（§2-206(1)(a)）、6月2日に到達したことは契約の成立を妨げない。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.23

questions.stem: On May 2, Mason orally contracted with Acme Appliances to buy for $480 a washer and dryer for household use. Mason and the Acme salesperson agreed that delivery would be made on July 2. On May 5, Mason telephoned Acme and requested that the delivery date be moved to June 2. The Acme salesperson agreed with this request. On June 2, Acme failed to deliver the washer and dryer to Mason because of an inventory shortage. Acme advised Mason that it would deliver the appliances on July 2 as originally agreed. Mason believes that Acme has breached its agreement with Mason. Acme contends that its agreement to deliver on June 2 was not binding. Acme's contention is

choices.label: A
choices.text: Correct, because Mason is not a merchant and was buying the appliances for household use.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Correct, because the agreement to change the delivery date was not in writing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Incorrect, because the agreement to change the delivery date was binding.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Incorrect, because Acme's agreement to change the delivery date is a firm offer that cannot be withdrawn by Acme.

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-209(1), an agreement modifying a contract for the sale of goods needs no consideration to be binding, provided it is made in good faith. Under §2-209(3), the modified contract must satisfy the Statute of Frauds only if the contract as modified falls within §2-201; because the price is $480, under the $500 threshold, the oral modification moving delivery to June 2 is enforceable, and Acme's failure to deliver on June 2 is a breach. Mason's status as a nonmerchant buying for household use is irrelevant, because §2-209(1) applies to merchants and nonmerchants alike. The lack of a writing does not matter because neither the original $480 contract nor the modification is subject to the Statute of Frauds. The modification is not a firm offer; a firm offer under §2-205 is an unaccepted offer by a merchant in a signed writing, whereas here Acme agreed to the change, creating a binding modified contract.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-209(1) により、物品売買契約の変更は、誠実になされる限り約因なしで拘束力をもつ。§2-209(3) により、変更後の契約が詐欺防止法の書面要件を満たす必要があるのは、変更後の契約が §2-201 の対象になる場合だけである。代金は$480で$500未満なので、引渡し日を6月2日に早める口頭の変更は有効であり、6月2日に引き渡さなかったAcmeは契約に違反している。§2-209(1) は商人・非商人を問わず適用されるので、Masonが家庭用に買う非商人であることは関係がない。元の契約も変更も詐欺防止法の対象外なので、書面がないことも問題にならない。ファーム・オファーは商人が署名付き書面でした未承諾の申込みであり（§2-205）、Acmeが変更に同意した本問の合意はそれに当たらない。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.24

questions.stem:
Which of the following conditions must be met for an implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose to arise in connection with a sale of goods?

I. The warranty must be in writing.
II. The seller must know that the buyer was relying on the seller in selecting the goods.

choices.label: A
choices.text: I only

choices.label: B
choices.text: II only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both I and II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither I nor II

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-315, an implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose arises when the seller, at the time of contracting, has reason to know any particular purpose for which the goods are required and that the buyer is relying on the seller's skill or judgment to select or furnish suitable goods. Statement II is therefore a required condition. Statement I is not required because the warranty is implied by law and needs no writing; only a disclaimer of the fitness warranty must be in writing and conspicuous (§2-316(2)). Therefore 'Both I and II' and 'I only' are incorrect, and 'Neither I nor II' ignores the buyer-reliance requirement.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-315 により、特定目的適合性の黙示保証は、売主が契約時に、物品が必要とされる特定の目的と、買主が適切な物品の選定を売主の技量・判断に頼っていることを知りうる場合に生じる。したがってIIは必要な条件である。この保証は法律上当然に生じるので書面は要らず、Iは条件ではない（書面で目立つ表示が必要なのは、この保証を排除する場合である（§2-316(2)））。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.25

questions.stem:
Which of the following factors result(s) in an express warranty with respect to a sale of goods?

I. The seller's description of the goods as part of the basis of the bargain.
II. The seller selects goods knowing the buyer's intended use.

choices.label: A
choices.text: I only

choices.label: B
choices.text: II only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both I and II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither I nor II

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-313(1)(b), any description of the goods that is made part of the basis of the bargain creates an express warranty that the goods will conform to the description; no formal words such as 'warrant' or 'guarantee' and no specific intention to make a warranty are needed (§2-313(2)). Statement I therefore creates an express warranty. Statement II does not create an express warranty: a seller selecting goods with knowledge of the buyer's intended use gives rise to the implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose under §2-315, which arises by law rather than from the seller's affirmations or descriptions. Therefore 'II only', 'Both I and II', and 'Neither I nor II' are incorrect.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-313(1)(b) により、取引の基礎（basis of the bargain）の一部となった物品の説明は、物品がその説明に合致するという明示の保証を生じる。'warrant' や 'guarantee' といった言葉や保証する意図は要らない（§2-313(2)）。したがってIは明示の保証を生じる。IIのように買主の使用目的を知って売主が物品を選ぶ場合に生じるのは、§2-315 の特定目的適合性の黙示保証であり、売主の言明や説明から生じる明示の保証ではない。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.27

questions.stem: Under the UCC Sales Article, the implied warranty of merchantability

choices.label: A
choices.text: May be disclaimed by a seller's oral statement that mentions merchantability.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Arises only in contracts involving a merchant seller and a merchant buyer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Is breached if the goods are not fit for all purposes for which the buyer intends to use the goods.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Must be part of the basis of the bargain to be binding on the seller.

questions.explanation: Under UCC §2-316(2), to exclude or modify the implied warranty of merchantability, the language must mention merchantability and, in the case of a writing, must be conspicuous. A writing is therefore not required, and an oral disclaimer that mentions merchantability is effective. The statement that the warranty arises only between a merchant seller and a merchant buyer is incorrect because §2-314 requires only that the seller be a merchant with respect to goods of that kind; the buyer need not be a merchant. The statement that the warranty is breached if the goods are not fit for all of the buyer's intended purposes is incorrect because merchantability requires fitness for the ordinary purposes for which such goods are used (§2-314(2)(c)); fitness for a buyer's particular purpose is a separate warranty under §2-315. The statement that the warranty must be part of the basis of the bargain is incorrect because that is the test for an express warranty (§2-313); the implied warranty of merchantability arises by operation of law.
questions.explanationJa: UCC §2-316(2) により、商品性の黙示保証を排除・修正するには merchantability に言及する必要があり、書面による場合は目立つ表示でなければならない。書面は必須ではないので、merchantability に言及した口頭の排除も有効である。§2-314 が求めるのは売主がその種類の物品を扱う商人であることだけで、買主は商人でなくてよい。商品性は、その種類の物品が通常使われる目的への適合性であり（§2-314(2)(c)）、買主が意図するすべての目的への適合性ではない（特定目的への適合性は §2-315 の別の保証）。取引の基礎の一部であることは明示の保証（§2-313）の要件で、商品性の黙示保証は法律上当然に生じる。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Sales Q.28
